sim.adapt.note.modal: Solves, then refines the elements where the mode shapes are least accurate (Zienkiewicz–Zhu estimate of every mode asked for, each counted alike) and solves again, until the estimate is under the target or the passes run out. On a part with only flat faces the frequencies can only go down from pass to pass; curved faces also get closer to their true shape, which can move them either way a little. The estimate is an estimate, not a bound.
sim.adapt.note.buckling: Solves, then refines the elements where the pre-stress and the buckling modes are least accurate (Zienkiewicz–Zhu, each counted alike) and solves again, until the estimate is under the target or the passes run out. Watch the load factor settle from pass to pass. The estimate is an estimate, not a bound.
sim.adapt.modal.units: Error estimate in % (all the modes asked for), natural frequencies in Hz.
sim.adapt.buckling.units: Error estimate in % (the pre-stress and the modes), load factors: the loads × this buckle.
sim.adapt.modal.chart: Estimated error and the first frequency against the number of unknowns, one point per pass (the table above has the numbers)
sim.adapt.buckling.chart: Estimated error and the first load factor against the number of unknowns, one point per pass (the table above has the numbers)
sim.adapt.modal.how: Each pass is a full solve on a mesh refined by conforming bisection where the estimate was largest.
sim.adapt.buckling.how: Each pass is a full solve (pre-stress, then the buckling modes) on a mesh refined by conforming bisection where the estimate was largest.
loft.rails.title: Guide rails (curves the sides follow)
loft.rails.note_off: Tick two or more curves (open sketches or model edges) that run from the first section to the last: the loft then passes through every section and along every rail.
loft.rails.note_on: With rails the loft is a Gordon surface through the sections and the rails, capped flat at both ends. Each rail must cross every section once (within 0.01 mm). Ruled and point or face sections do not apply.
loft.rails.report: Follows the sections and the {n} rails within {dev} mm.
loft.rails.sketches_only: With guide rails every section must be a sketch (a point or a face cannot take a rail).
loft.rails.two: Guide rails need two or more curves; with one, leave it out or add another.

sheet.err.profile: A base flange needs a closed profile (a plate) or one open chain of lines (a bent sheet).
sheet.err.no_body: There is no sheet yet to add a flange to.
sheet.err.pick_edge: Pick a straight edge of the sheet for the flange.
sheet.err.edge_gone: The edge it uses is gone: the edge between {a} and {b}.
sheet.err.straight: An edge flange needs a straight edge.
sheet.err.planar: The flange's edge must join two flat faces of the sheet.
sheet.err.square: The flange's edge must be a square edge of the sheet (its two faces at 90°).
sheet.err.thickness: That edge is not on a face of the sheet's thickness ({t}): pick an edge of the top or bottom face.
sheet.err.offsets: The offsets leave nothing of the edge ({len} long).
sheet.err.zero_line: A line of the profile has no length.
sheet.err.straight_on: Two lines of the profile run straight on: join them into one.
sheet.err.fold_back: A corner of the profile folds right back (180°): a bend needs room to turn.
sheet.err.short_leg: Line {n} of the profile is {len} long, shorter than its bends need ({need}): lengthen it or use a smaller radius.
sheet.menu.base.title: Sheet metal: a plate from a closed sketch, or a bent sheet from an open chain of lines (sets the thickness, bend radius and K-factor; exact kernel)
sheet.menu.flange.title: Sheet metal: bend a flange up from a straight edge of the sheet, with bend reliefs (exact kernel)
sheet.ui.needs_exact: Sheet metal needs the exact kernel (OpenCascade), which is not loaded yet. Try again in a moment.
sheet.ui.no_sketch: Make a sketch first: a closed profile for a plate, or an open chain of lines for a bent sheet.
sheet.ui.pick_status: Click a straight edge of the sheet's top or bottom face for {name}. Esc cancels.
sheet.ui.pick_straight: Click a straight edge of the sheet.
sheet.ui.reverse: Thickness outside the bends (the sketch is the inside face)
sheet.ui.base_note: A closed sketch makes a plate this thick. An open chain of lines makes a bent sheet: every corner becomes a bend of this inside radius, and the sheet is Depth long. The flanges after it use this thickness, radius and K-factor.
sheet.ui.flip: Bend the other way (from the other face)
sheet.ui.from_base: Bent with {name}'s sheet: {t} mm thick, inside radius {r} mm, K-factor {k}. Length is the flat leg past the bend; a relief is cut beside each end you offset.
sheet.flat.no_base: There is no sheet metal to lay flat: the part needs a base flange that builds.
sheet.flat.first_base: The part has more than one base flange; this is the flat of the first, {name}.
sheet.flat.bent_flanges: Edge flanges on a bent base flange cannot be laid flat yet. Start from a flat plate to unfold flanges.
sheet.flat.bent_cuts: Cuts and holes made after a bent base flange are not shown in its flat yet.
sheet.flat.no_plate: The flat sheet's face could not be found on the base flange's sketch plane.
sheet.flat.leg_gone: {name}'s flange face is gone, so it cannot be laid flat.
sheet.flat.fuse: The flat pieces could not be joined into one outline.
sheet.flat.title: Flat pattern
sheet.flat.lay_title: Unfold the sheet: the outline with its holes and reliefs, and the bend lines
sheet.flat.dxf_title: Save the flat pattern as DXF (R12, mm): the outline on OUTLINE, bend lines on BEND (dashed) with notes on BEND_NOTES
configs.err.name: A configuration has no name, or the same name as another.
configs.err.unknown: Configuration {name} sets {param}, but the part has no parameter of that name.
configs.err.number: Configuration {name}: the value of {param} is not a number.
configs.err.many: A part keeps {n} configurations at most.
configs.err.missing: Configuration {name} sets {param}, which is no longer a parameter of the part.
configs.err.taken: There is already a configuration called {name}.
configs.title: Configurations
configs.empty: No configurations yet. Set the parameters for one size of the part, type a name below and save it; or import a CSV design table (a name column and one column per parameter).
configs.need_params: Add the parameters first: a configuration sets parameters by name.
configs.need_name: Type a name for the configuration first.
configs.imported: Saved {n} configurations from {file} in the part. Apply one to set its values.
configs.nothing: There are no parameters to put in a table.
configs.exported_current: Exported the current values as a one-row design table: add rows in a spreadsheet and import it.
configs.apply_title: Set the parameters to this configuration's values
configs.update_title: Save the current parameter values into this configuration
configs.delete_title: Delete this configuration (the parameters keep their values)
configs.import_title: Add the rows of a CSV design table as configurations (a row with an existing name replaces it)
asm.joint.note.rigid: Rigid: the parts are held together at this angle and offset.
asm.joint.note.revolute: Revolute: the second part turns about the joint's axis (square to the faces). Drag the angle to check the motion.
asm.joint.note.slider: Slider: the second part slides along the joint's axis. Drag the offset to check the motion.
asm.joint.note.cylindrical: Cylindrical: the second part turns about the joint's axis and slides along it, like a shaft in a plain bearing.
asm.joint.note.planar: Planar: the second part stays face to face with the first, sliding in X and Y across the face and turning about the axis square to it.
asm.joint.note.ball: Ball: the second part turns every way about the joint's centre (where the faces meet): a spin about the axis and two tilts.
asm.joint.note.pinslot: Pin in slot: the second part slides along a straight slot in the first face (its direction set by Slot direction, from the face's X) and turns about the pin's axis.
asm.joint.check_bad: {n} of {of} positions clash, first at {value} {at} ({vol} mm³).
asm.joint.check_ok: No clash anywhere for {value} from {from} to {to} ({n} positions checked).
asm.limits.title: Limits
asm.limits.err_name: A joint's limits name a value it does not have.
asm.limits.err_bad: A joint's limits are bad (the minimum must be below the maximum).
asm.limits.err_range: A joint's limits are out of range.
rib.err.no_body: A rib needs a body to meet: build the part's walls first.
rib.err.profile: A rib needs one open chain of lines in its sketch (one line, or several end to end).
rib.err.build: The rib could not be made from this.
rib.err.inside: The rib's edge runs inside the body there: draw it in the open space between the walls.
rib.err.open: On this side the rib's edge never meets the body. Tick Flip to fill the other side, or move the line so walls close it in.
rib.menu.title: A rib (gusset) from an open sketch line: fills the sketch plane from the line to the walls, a set thickness across it (exact kernel)
rib.ui.no_sketch: Draw the rib's edge first: a sketch with one line (or a chain of lines) between the walls, on the plane the rib lies in.
rib.ui.added: {name} added. Set its thickness and side on the right.
rib.ui.flipped: {name} added, filling the side the walls close in (Flip is ticked).
rib.ui.side.front: In front of the plane (along its normal)
rib.ui.flip: Flip: fill the other side of the line
rib.ui.note: The rib fills the sketch plane from its line to the body, on the side toward the body's centre (Flip: the other side). The line's ends are carried on until they meet the walls.
draft.menu.title: Colour the part by its draft angle against a pull direction: where it releases from a mould and where it needs draft (Design)
draft.title: Draft analysis
draft.close.title: Stop the draft analysis (Esc)
draft.pick.hint: Click a flat face: the pull runs square to it, out of the part. Esc cancels.
draft.class.negative: Negative draft ({min}° or more the other way)
draft.note: Faces turned toward the pull release from that half of the mould; faces turned away release from the other half. Walls with less than the minimum draft need draft added.
draft.blocked: Draft analysis works on the part in the Design workspace (not in a sketch, a drawing or an assembly).
draft.no_part: There is no part to analyse yet.
draft.need_flat: Click a flat face of the part to set the pull square to it.
cs.file.unknown: {name}: PartCraft scripts read .craft, .lua and .py scripts and STL, OBJ, CSV, JSON, NPY and HDF5 data.
cs.drop.hint: Drop a script (.craft, .lua, .py), a data file, or a part
cs.open.title: Open a script (.craft, .lua, .py) or load a data file (STL, OBJ, CSV, JSON, NPY, HDF5) into the variables
cs.python.err.load: Python (CPython for WebAssembly) did not load.
cs.python.err.deep_out: Value nested too deeply for Python.
cs.python.err.field: "{name}" is not a valid field name.
cs.python.err.value: This Python value cannot be passed to CraftScript.
cs.python.err.assign: A {type} cannot be assigned into from Python.
cs.python.err.var: "{name}" is not a valid variable name.
cs.python.err.gone: A value from an earlier run is gone; compute it again.
gordon.err.no_boundary: No boundary curve of the network lies in the plane to be tangent to (the nearest is {d} mm off it; the tolerance is {tol} mm).
gordon.err.same_boundary: Two planes touch the same boundary curve of the network.
gordon.tangent: tangent along {curve} to its plane (it met it at up to {angle}°)
gordon.ui.title: Tangent to
gordon.ui.none: None: the surface meets its neighbours along the boundary curves without matching their slope.
gordon.ui.add_face_title: Pick a flat face in the view first; the surface leaves the boundary curve lying in it tangent to it
gordon.ui.note: For each plane, the boundary curve of the network lying in it is found, and the surface leaves that curve tangent to the plane (G1): a mirror plane or a flat face it grows from. Guides that leave that curve tangent to the plane are followed exactly; others are bent near it, and the report says by how much.
analysis.menu.zebra.title: Reflection stripes on the part: smooth across tangent joins, broken at creases (Design)
analysis.menu.curvature.title: Colour the part by its mean curvature: concave blue, flat pale, convex red (Design)
analysis.zebra.note: Stripes of a reflected light pattern, redrawn as you turn the view. Where two faces join smoothly (tangent) the stripes run on with a bend; at a crease they break.
analysis.curv.note: Mean curvature at each point of the mesh; the colours reach full strength at ±{lim} 1/mm (a radius of {rad} mm). Sharp edges count as very curved.
drawing.holes.title: Hole table ({view} view)
file.drawing.holes_bad: The hole table settings in this file are bad.
drawing.holes.skipped: {n} more are not square to that view.
drawing.holes.exact: The hole table needs the exact kernel (the mesh kernel has no hole faces).
cam.adaptive.err.tool: Adaptive clearing needs an end mill (flat, ball or bull nose).
cam.adaptive.err.pick: Pick the area to clear: a flat floor face, a round hole or a closed chain of edges.
cam.adaptive.warn.nothing: Nothing to cut in the {what}: its top is at or below its bottom.
cam.adaptive.warn.fit: The tool (⌀{d}) does not fit in the {what}.
cam.adaptive.label: Adaptive
cam.adaptive.title: Adaptive clearing: pick the floor face or a hole; passes that keep the cutter's engagement to a set width, so it can cut deeper and faster
cam.adaptive.engagement: Engagement (× diameter): the width each pass cuts
cam.adaptive.err.fit: The tool does not fit in this pocket.
kernel.chip.mesh.title: manifold-3d builds the part as a mesh: round faces are flat facets (Curves sets how fine). Fillets, shells, sweeps, surfaces and the other exact-only features are not built yet.
kernel.not_built: {what}: not built yet. It needs an exact kernel, which this version of PartCraft does not have. Help › What is not built yet says what to do instead.
kernel.not_built.short: not built yet (needs an exact kernel)
kernel.step.not_built: Exact STEP: not built yet (it needs an exact kernel). "STEP (faceted)" writes the part as flat facets, which CAD programs open.
kernel.part.note: Round faces are flat facets: "Curves" sets how fine. Volumes and areas are of the faceted solid, a little low.
kernel.drawing.status: Drawing (curves are drawn as facets). Datum, Frame and Finish place GD&T on a view; the panel sets a section and a detail view.
kernel.feature.not_built: {label}: not built yet. It needs an exact kernel, which this version of PartCraft does not have.
kernel.mesh.named_face: It sits on a face only an exact kernel can find: not built yet in this version.
kernel.mesh.extrude_to: Extruding up to a face, the next face or a vertex: not built yet (it needs an exact kernel).
kernel.mesh.taper: A taper: not built yet (it needs an exact kernel).
kernel.mesh.pattern_bodies: Patterning bodies: not built yet (it needs an exact kernel; the mesh kernel keeps one solid).
kernel.mesh.ref_face: It uses a face or edge of the solid, which only an exact kernel can find: not built yet in this version.
kernel.mesh.new_body: A new body: not built yet (it needs an exact kernel; the mesh kernel keeps one solid).
kernel.what.form_check: Checking a form as an exact solid
touch.add.title: Taps add to the selection or take out, like Shift+click. Tap again to stop.
touch.done.title: Finish the line, spline or polygon you are drawing, like a right-click.
touch.esc.title: Cancel or step back, like the Esc key.
touch.long_press: Hold a finger still: in a sketch it finishes what you draw, or with Select adds the item to the selection.

app.clip.sketch_pasted: Pasted {what}{relations}{dropped}. Drag it, or add relations to tie it in.

app.settings.orbit_left: Left-drag turns the part again; right or middle drag pans.
app.settings.autorel_on: Drawing adds coincident, horizontal and vertical relations again.

app.settings.bed_bad: Give the bed's width, depth and height in millimeters, each from 10 to 5000.
app.print3d.title: Check for 3D printing
app.print3d.what.part: What prints: the part, standing as it is in the view (Y up becomes the printer's Z).
app.print3d.what.asm: What prints: the whole assembly, every copy where it is placed.
app.print3d.size: Size: {w} × {d} × {h} mm (X × Y × Z on the bed).
app.print3d.nobed: Bed size: not set (Settings › PartCraft › 3D printer).
app.print3d.ready: Ready to print: closed all round, faces the right way out, nothing passing through itself.
app.print3d.notready: Not ready to print: a slicer may refuse it or print it wrong.

app.print3d.p.open.other: {n} edges have a face on one side only: there are holes.

app.print3d.p.nonmanifold.other: {n} edges are shared by three or more faces.

app.print3d.p.flipped.other: {n} edges lie between faces facing opposite ways.

app.print3d.p.selfintersect.other: A body passes through itself in {n} places.

app.print3d.w.overlap.one: Separate bodies overlap in {n} place. Slicers usually merge them; Combine joins them for a cleaner file.
app.print3d.w.overlap.other: Separate bodies overlap in {n} places. Slicers usually merge them; Combine joins them for a cleaner file.

app.print3d.w.touch.one: Bodies meet face to face along {n} edge. Slicers usually join them.
app.print3d.w.touch.other: Bodies meet face to face along {n} edges. Slicers usually join them.

app.print3d.w.tiny: It is under 1 mm across. Check the part's sizes.
app.print3d.w.bed: It is larger than your printer's bed ({x} × {y} × {z} mm), even turned on the bed.
app.print3d.w.nobase: Nothing lies flat at the bottom: turn the part so a face rests on the bed (in your slicer), or it will need supports or a raft.
app.print3d.w.overhang: {share}% of the surface leans out more than {angle}° from upright and will need support, standing as it is.

app.print3d.w.degenerate.one: {n} triangle with no area is left out.
app.print3d.w.degenerate.other: {n} triangles with no area are left out.

app.pick.multi_edges.other: {n} edges picked. Fillet or Chamfer rounds them; Shift+click picks more, Esc clears.

app.sketch.no_plane: This sketch has no plane to sit on.

app.feature.added_refs: {name} added. Set its references on the right (Pick buttons take a click in the view).
app.feature.needs_exact_loading: {what}s need the exact kernel (OpenCascade), which is still loading. Try again in a moment.
app.feature.needs_exact_off: {what}s need the exact kernel (OpenCascade), which is not loaded.

app.feature.added_edges.one: {name} added ({n} edge). Change its size on the right; Pick edges changes which.

app.props.head: Properties
app.props.base_plane: A base plane through the origin.
app.props.multi_edges_note: Shift+click adds or drops edges. Fillet or Chamfer makes the feature with all of them.
app.props.multi_faces_note: Shift+click adds or drops faces. Shell hollows the part with these faces open.
app.edge.note_line: Shift+click picks more edges first. A straight edge can also set a pattern's direction or axis (choose "Picked edge" in its panel).
app.edge.note_mesh: A straight edge can set a linear pattern's direction or a circular pattern's axis: pick it, then add the pattern (or choose "Picked edge" in its panel).
app.props.name: Name
app.part.note_exact: The exact kernel keeps true circles, cylinders and cones: volumes and STEP are exact. "Curves" sets how finely the view, STL and 3MF are tessellated.
app.part.note_mesh_loading: Circles and arcs are faceted for the solid: "Curves" sets how finely. Volumes are of the faceted solid (the exact kernel is loading).
app.part.note_mesh_off: Circles and arcs are faceted for the solid: "Curves" sets how finely. Volumes are of the faceted solid (the exact kernel is not loaded).
app.part.start_note: Pick a plane or a flat face and choose Sketch to start. Click a feature in the history to change it.
app.face.fixed_note: This face was not made by a sketch edge, so a sketch on it stays where the face is now and will not follow later changes.

app.dims.angle_range: An angle is between 0 and 180 degrees.

app.feature.suppressed_msg: Suppressed: not built. Features that need it are not built either.

app.feature.picking_edges: Picking: the part is shown as it is before {name}. Click edges to add or drop them; Done (or Esc) builds it.

app.pattern.full_circle: Equal spacing all the way round.
app.pattern.spread: The copies spread over this angle.

app.seeds.whole_body: The whole body (as built so far)

ui.settings.threads.hint: Large simulation models solve faster on several threads; small ones stay on one (starting threads costs more than it saves). Automatic uses one thread fewer than the computer has, so the page stays responsive.

gen.intro: Grow shapes from goals: pick the faces that are held and loaded, regions to keep and to keep clear, a target volume and materials. Each outcome is the stiffest shape found for its volume (topology optimisation), checked again as a solid, and shown as a smooth surface you can download.

gen.method: Method: topology optimisation for stiffness (SIMP, penalty 3, density filter, threshold projection, optimality criteria) on a voxel mesh, linear static, one material at a time. The faces you load or fix are kept solid; frictionless faces are not (they are often symmetry planes). Each outcome keeps its target volume, is checked again as a solid with the real material, and is smoothed into a closed faceted surface. There are no stress limits or manufacturing rules (overhangs, milling directions) yet: check an outcome in Simulation before trusting it.

study.ws.tet_note: Mesh: 10-node quadratic tetrahedra fitted to the exact faces (isosurface stuffing on a graded lattice, refined near curved faces, thin walls and sharp edges; boundary and midside nodes on the exact surfaces of planes, cylinders, cones, spheres, tori, revolved and extruded faces and B-spline faces, other faces follow their display mesh), solved by conjugate gradients with an algebraic multigrid preconditioner. Linear elastic, small displacements, isotropic material (3D-printed plastics are weaker across layers). Stresses are averaged at the nodes; at sharp inside corners and at the edges of fixed faces they are singular and grow as the mesh is refined: read them a little away.
study.ws.voxel_note: Method: linear elastic, small displacements, isotropic material (3D-printed plastics are weaker across layers). The part is filled with equal cubes (8-node hexahedra, incompatible modes by default) so curved faces become a staircase; stresses at sharp inside corners and at the edges of fixed faces grow as the cubes shrink (they are singular) — read stresses a little away from them. Solved by conjugate gradients with a multigrid preconditioner.

study.adapt.heading: Automatic refinement
study.adapt.note_thermal: Solves, then refines the elements with the largest estimated error and solves again, until the estimated error is under the target or the passes run out. The estimate (Zienkiewicz–Zhu) is an estimate, not a bound, and it covers the whole part (energy norm): a peak flux usually needs a target under 1 %. It never settles at sharp inside corners or the edges of fixed faces, where the true value is infinite.
study.adapt.note_stress: Solves, then refines the elements with the largest estimated error and solves again, until the estimated error is under the target or the passes run out. The estimate (Zienkiewicz–Zhu) is an estimate, not a bound, and it covers the whole part (energy norm): a peak stress usually needs a target under 1 %. It never settles at sharp inside corners or the edges of fixed faces, where the true value is infinite.

study.flow.turb_warning: Experimental: this turbulence model did not pass its accuracy checks. Measured errors: flat channels, friction +3 to +5 % (Dean, first cell at y⁺ 49–98); resolved-wall channel, bulk velocity −1 % (Moser et al., y⁺ ≈ 3); pipe friction 30 to 34 % too high; reattachment behind a backward-facing step 21 to 39 % too short; results improve only slowly with finer cells. Use it for qualitative flow patterns (where flow separates, recirculates or speeds up), not for design numbers.

study.flow.ui.method_laminar: Method: laminar, incompressible, isothermal flow of a Newtonian fluid, solved by the lattice Boltzmann method (D3Q19, two-relaxation-time collision) on equal cubic cells, run to a steady state. Walls are no-slip (interpolated bounce-back follows curved walls; bounce-back makes them a staircase); inlets set a uniform velocity, outlets a static pressure. Above a Reynolds number of about 2,000 in pipes (or once a wake starts to shed) real flow is unsteady or turbulent and these results do not hold: use the turbulent flow model there. Flow and pressures are gauge values; the fluid's density and viscosity are constant (no heat, no cavitation, no gravity). Openings smaller than a few cells are poorly resolved. Lab build: check important results another way.
study.flow.ui.method_turb: Method (experimental): turbulent, incompressible, isothermal flow of a Newtonian fluid as a steady RANS solution — the time-averaged flow, not its fluctuations. The Spalart–Allmaras one-equation model (finite volumes on the same cells) gives an eddy viscosity that the lattice Boltzmann method (D3Q19, two-relaxation-time collision) uses cell by cell. The cells next to walls use Spalding's law of the wall instead of resolving the thin layer there, imposed as a slip velocity on the wall links. The model is fully turbulent everywhere (no laminar regions, no transition), assumes equilibrium boundary layers at the walls, and has an isotropic eddy viscosity. A small Smagorinsky stabilizer acts only where the grid sees gradients the model does not cover (sharp inlet corners, the start of the run). Inlets carry 5 % turbulence (external flow: 1 %). It did not pass its accuracy checks: see the warning above and the help topic.

Pick the flat face around an opening (the rim of a pipe end, a port face): its holes are closed by a lid there, so every hole of that face belongs to the opening. Or model a thin cap over the opening, as in other CAD tools, and pick its inner face. Every opening needs one; a wall thinner than the cell size can leak.

study.flow.ui.w.lam_pipe_turb: Reynolds number {re}: pipe flow at this Reynolds number is turbulent. The laminar model does not describe the real flow (pressure drop is underestimated): use the turbulent flow model.
study.flow.ui.w.mach: The fastest flow reaches lattice Mach {mach}: the method's compressibility errors grow above about 0.3. Smaller cells or a lower step limit on speed help.
study.flow.ui.w.sa_ext_laminar: Reynolds number {re}: the flow around the part is laminar here. The turbulent model treats it as fully turbulent; use the laminar model.
study.flow.ui.w.sa_ext_trans: Reynolds number {re}: on a real part the boundary layers start laminar and turn turbulent somewhere along it (around 5 × 10⁵ on a smooth flat face). This model has no transition: it treats them as turbulent from the front, which raises friction drag and misses effects such as the drag crisis of round bodies.
study.flow.ui.w.sa_pipe_laminar: Reynolds number {re}: pipe flow at this Reynolds number is laminar. The turbulent model treats it as fully turbulent and over-predicts friction and pressure drop; use the laminar model.
study.flow.ui.w.sa_pipe_trans: Reynolds number {re}: transitional (2,300–4,000 in pipes). The turbulent model assumes fully turbulent flow; the real friction lies between the laminar and turbulent values.
study.flow.ui.w.sa_unsteady: The run did not settle. Behind a bluff body the real flow sheds vortices; a steady RANS run then has no steady answer, and these numbers are one moment of a moving flow.
study.flow.ui.w.yplus_buffer: Most first cells sit in the buffer layer (median y⁺ {med}, between the viscous sublayer and the log layer), where this wall treatment was least accurate in the checks (friction up to about 20 % high). Larger cells (y⁺ 30–300) or much smaller ones (y⁺ ≤ 3) are better.
study.flow.ui.w.yplus_high: First-cell y⁺ reaches {max}, above the {hi} this wall treatment was checked to ({pct} % of the wall cells): the wall law is out of its range there. Use smaller cells.
study.flow.ui.w.yplus_low: First-cell y⁺ falls to {min}, below {lo} ({pct} % of the wall cells — usually stagnation and separation points, where the wall law is approximate anyway).

study.thermal.note.field: Add fixed temperatures, convection and the like below: the steady temperatures are solved first on the same mesh, then the part expands by α·(T − stress-free temperature).
study.thermal.stress_at.worst: The worst time (stress over the whole run)
study.thermal.note.worst: Add fixed temperatures, convection and the like below. The temperatures are solved over time from the start temperature on the same mesh; then a static solve at each of the stress solves, spread evenly over the run (the start included), gives the stress history, its peak and when it happens. Fixed temperatures apply from the first instant (a sudden change): the stress right at the start depends on the element size.
study.thermal.note.time: Add fixed temperatures, convection and the like below. The temperatures are solved over time from the start temperature on the same mesh, up to the time step nearest the chosen time; the part then expands by α·(T − stress-free temperature) at that instant.
study.thermal.method.steady: Method: heat conduction, linear (constant conductivity, density and specific heat), steady state, on the same cube mesh (8-node hexahedra), solved by conjugate gradients with an incomplete Cholesky preconditioner. Flux and convection act on the faces' true area. Radiation goes to the surroundings only (no face-to-face exchange) and is linearised, h = εσ(T² + T∞²)(T + T∞), re-solved until it settles. Convection coefficients are inputs (there is no fluid flow here). No contact resistance. The heat balance (in versus out) checks each solve. Lab build: check important parts another way.
study.thermal.method.transient: Method: heat conduction, linear (constant conductivity, density and specific heat), transient by {scheme} time steps from a uniform start temperature, on the same cube mesh (8-node hexahedra), solved by conjugate gradients with an incomplete Cholesky preconditioner. Flux and convection act on the faces' true area. Radiation goes to the surroundings only (no face-to-face exchange) and is linearised, h = εσ(T² + T∞²)(T + T∞), re-solved until it settles. Convection coefficients are inputs (there is no fluid flow here). No contact resistance. The heat balance (in versus out) checks each solve. Lab build: check important parts another way.
study.thermal.method.buckling: Method: linear (eigenvalue) buckling. A static solve under the loads gives the pre-stress; then (K + λKσ)φ = 0 is solved for the lowest load factors λ by subspace iteration (K: the cube mesh's stiffness, Kσ: the geometric stiffness of the pre-stress). Linear buckling overestimates real buckling loads: real parts have imperfections, residual stresses and yielding, and thin shells can buckle well below this value. Use a margin. A load factor below 1 means it buckles under the applied load. Lab build: check important parts another way.
study.thermal.note.static: Thermal load: the material expands by α·ΔT (linear, α constant); stresses are σ = D(ε − α ΔT). Thermal loads are self-balanced, so the reactions still balance only the mechanical loads.
study.thermal.note.static_transient: Over time: quasi-static (no inertia), one linear static solve per stress time on the transient temperatures (k, ρ, cp, E, ν, α constant).
study.thermal.status.solved: Solved: temperature {lo} to {hi} °C, heat in {q} W ({els}).
study.thermal.status.solved_at: Solved: temperature {lo} to {hi} °C at {time} s, heat in {q} W ({els}).
study.thermal.status.buckles: Lowest buckling load factor {l}: it buckles under the applied load ({els}).

study.thermal.val.eig_converged: converged in {n} subspace iterations ({solves} stiffness solves{residual}), {sec} s{threads}
study.thermal.val.eig_not_converged: NOT converged in {n} subspace iterations ({solves} stiffness solves{residual}), {sec} s{threads}
study.thermal.msg.not_settled: The load factors did not settle: treat them as rough, try fewer modes or a coarser mesh.
study.thermal.msg.below_one: The lowest load factor is {l}, below 1: the part buckles under the applied load.
study.thermal.note.buckling: Linear buckling overestimates the load at which a real part buckles (imperfections, residual stress, yielding): use a generous margin. A load factor is the multiple of the applied loads at which the ideal part buckles. Shapes are scaled to 1 at their largest motion; their size and sign mean nothing.
study.thermal.note.balance: Heat in and out are summed over every condition (a fixed temperature counts what it must supply or absorb). The imbalance shows how well the solve closed; a large one means the result is not to be trusted.
